🚨 *new alert — needs human* — group `c5773f0cfb4566e3`
Channel: #swat  •  confidence: 0.50  •  bug-type guess: env (infra)  •  alerts in group: 10

*Deviation note:* prompt says swat → thread-reply on primary alert. I deferred — incident already resolved (Arash all-clear at 12:00:52Z, ~7 min before I polled), cron has been silent since 2026-05-13T22:12Z (14h+), and posting bot-output into a closed P0 thread from a manual local run felt low-value/high-noise. React 👎 if you want me to post the thread reply anyway and I'll do it next cycle.

*Symptoms (window 11:44Z → 12:01Z):*
  - Tables & Fields 500 errors on **QBO-only** accounts (create table/field, T&F dropdowns in Manage App). QBDT path unaffected per Inder's Jira description.
  - Intermittent signin 500s — "Error Code: 500-Authentication Failure". Partial: Inder could sign in, Nelson couldn't, then recovered.
  - Self-resolved in ~13 min.

*Trace IDs:* n/a — DD APM unavailable from this run env.

*Likely cause (low confidence):* shared upstream infra blip
  1. SQL cluster failover on the QBO+AlocetSystem cluster — best fit for QBO-only T&F scoping + partial signin
  2. `microservices` IIS pool recycle — partial fit (doesn't explain signin alone)
  3. Redis JWT-cache hiccup — partial fit (doesn't explain QBO-only T&F)

*Deploy correlation:* none. Zero commits in the 4h window across `ms-tables-fields-api`, `ms-authentication-api`, `ms-gateway-api`, `oauth2`, `method-signin-ui`, `runtime-core`, `method-platform-ui`. Most recent on any of these is `runtime-core` 1f179c6d2 (8d ago).

*Suggested next action:* retro investigation with DD/ES once cron-host tooling is back. Restore cron secrets/VPN on the cron host — this incident landed inside the cron-outage window and we're flying blind on a real P0.

🚨 *new alert — needs human* — group `113ac8b38c9e8e00`
Channel: #alert-system  •  confidence: 0.50  •  bug-type guess: env (infra)  •  alerts in group: 40

*Symptoms (window 11:41Z → 12:05Z, 23 min 36 s):*
  - 40 alerts from 3 distinct bots: Centreon Monitoring (B03GBAMHUTB, 30 msgs), B011R3D650X (7), B05PN7JG87L (2)
  - All messages have empty `text` (content is in Slack blocks/attachments — invisible to `conversations.history` in the format the bot reads)
  - Volume burst is well above prior poll-cycle baseline (last cycle 2026-05-13T22:12Z showed `polled: 7`)
  - First Centreon fire at 11:41:56Z — *3 min before* the swat user-impact reports started at 11:44:53Z

*Trace IDs:* n/a — content not visible.

*Likely cause:* same as swat P0 group `c5773f0cfb4566e3` — shared upstream infra blip. Centreon's 3-min lead time suggests low-level metric detection (TCP probe, IIS health, SQL TCP, disk/CPU) before user impact surfaced.

*Suggested next action:* fix routine's Slack-payload parsing to fall back to `attachments[0].title` / `blocks[*].elements[*].text` when `text` is empty. This is the single highest-leverage triage-bot improvement — currently we lose ~95% of Centreon's signal.

*Grouping note:* strict reading of the bot-id heuristic would split this into 4+ subgroups (one per bot_id transition). I clustered as one because all 40 share channel + empty text_fingerprint + 23-min window (< 30-min threshold), and they timing-correlate with the swat P0. Erring toward fewer-DMs as the prompt allows ("note both in single DM rather than splitting").

🚨 *new alert — needs human* — group `c211463713c5a280`
Channel: #alert-runtime-monitoring  •  confidence: 0.40  •  bug-type guess: env (infra)  •  alerts in group: 2

*Symptoms (window 12:00:36Z → 12:04:59Z):*
  - 2 alerts from B063S8NBW0M, 4 min 23 s apart
  - Both have empty `text` (Slack-block content not visible)
  - Both land in the *swat-recovery window* — first one is 16 s before Arash's "back to normal" call

*Trace IDs:* n/a.

*Likely cause:* lagged echo of the swat P0 group `c5773f0cfb4566e3`. `runtime-core` depends on `ms-tables-fields-api` for table/field metadata; a tables-fields outage surfaces as runtime-core errors with a few-minute lag as request queues drain.

Lower-confidence alternative: an independent runtime-core background-job failure unrelated to the outage. Can't distinguish without block content or DD/ES.

*Suggested next action:* same as Group B — fix block-content parsing. Once visible, this group likely either folds into the swat investigation (confirmation of cascading-failure pattern) or surfaces as a separate signal worth higher-frequency polling.
